key: ‘Thou knowest how that David my father could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.
s: Sending to Hiram of Tyre for cedars, Solomon explains why the Temple falls to him; Radak, on 5:17, reads the wars as the apparent reason, Solomon keeping from Hiram that God had withheld the task from David, since telling it would not honour his father.

reason: Opened packet.js tanakh 107 --verse 5.17: Radak on מפני המלחמה writes לא רצה לגלות לו הטעם כי האל מנעו כי לא היה כבוד אביו ואמר לו זה הטעם הנרא'. The problem holds: ‘which would not honour his father’ attached to God’s withholding the task, whereas in Radak the dishonour lies in revealing that reason (he did not wish to reveal it, for it was not his father’s honour). Corrected only that clause, as the critic proposed: ‘since telling it would not honour his father’.
